candidates.text:
Every growth marketer I know who got fired over the last 12 months made the same mistake: they optimized for quality instead of speed.

They spend three months designing the perfect landing page, filming high-production videos, designing fancy ads, and building out a full nurture flow. Then they launch. It flops. And they start over.

In 2026, this will kill you. In growth, 80% of your initiatives will fail. Full stop. So if you dedicate resources to making each one “beautiful”, you're allocating unnecessary effort to initiatives that won't exist in three months. This slows you down A LOT.

Instead, spend as much time as possible on the one thing you cannot improvise: narrative. ICP, pain point, solution, overall pitch. This is 90%+ of what will determine the success of your campaign.

Everything else is a nice-to-have you layer on after you've found what works. The reality is that NOBODY CARES if your videos are in 4K at 60fps or shot on an iPhone. 

As an example, Clay’s best performing Meta ad right now is a screenshot and a few lines of text we pulled together in 5 minutes!

People buy your product for one of two reasons: it makes them money or it saves them money. Switching costs are close to zero nowadays.

So why would your ICP care about your video production quality or your landing page design? They don't. They care about one thing: does this solution help me solve my problem?

A raw pitch with the right angle beats a polished pitch with the wrong message every single time. And the only way to find the right angle is to experiment a lot and find what works.

Test ICP → pain point → use case. Iterate until you find early signs of success. Then improve the quality of the campaign. That's how you keep your job in the era of AI.

Frontier markets are being talked about far more than when we first started, and the trading of compute is leading the way.

Physical Markets go far beyond compute, to the data centres and energy infrastructure being consolidated into the hands of the few who want to control this new era. Soon, some of you will be part of it too.

Early next week, I hope to publish the fullest picture yet of how I see this unfolding: what Physical Markets are, and why this primitive will become the holy grail for tokenisation, financial markets and the interconnected economy at large.

On any given low-ticket offer the upsell take rate is going to be the determining factor of your high-ticket buyers. 

About 80% of your high-ticket buyers are going to be upsell-one buyers. 

These are known as double buyers. 

They buy the front end, then they buy the upsell, so they want to get the solution twice. This tells you the emotional investment they have in the outcome.

Which increases the probability of buying something else the third time, which is the high-ticket backend.

Your upsell one take rate should be 20% to 30% at least.
